raw_case_text: A 25-year-old woman was admitted to a local hospital 2 years ago because of facial and lower limb edema. On admission, the patient had abnormal renal function with serum creatinine 150 mumol/L (normal range: 41.00-81.00 mumol/L) and 24-h urine protein excretion was 12.77 g. Laboratory examination showed positive ANA, anti-double-stranded DNA (dsDNA), anti-Sm antibody, anti-U1RNP antibody, and mild reduction of complement C3. Renal histopathology indicated LN (class IV + V); the activity index was 9, and the chronic index was 1. Methylprednisolone (500 mg/day) pulse therapy was administered thrice. Subsequently, multitarget treatments were administered, including prednisone 30 mg/day, mycophenolate mofetil (MMF) 1,000 mg/day, and tacrolimus 2 mg/day. After treatment for 4 months, anti-dsDNA and anti-ANA antibodies were negative, serum creatinine decreased from 150 mumol/L to 73 mumol/L, and the urine protein-to-creatinine ratio decreased from 5,665 mg/gCr to 3,526 mg/gCr. Due to concerns about infection, MMF was stopped, and tacrolimus was adjusted to 4 mg/day, combined with hydroxychloroquine (HCQ) (200 mg/day). After 6 months of therapy, the patient's urine protein-to-creatinine ratio and serum albumin (ALB) were in a range of 3,834.33-8,590.89 mg/gCr and 22.7-32.8 g/L, respectively. In the seventh month of treatment, the patient developed fever and cough, procalcitonin (PCT) and C-reactive protein (CRP) levels increased, and cytomegalovirus (CMV)-IgM was positive. Chest CT and blood next-generation sequencing results suggested that the patient had Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia. Tacrolimus and prednisone were discontinued and methylprednisolone (8 mg/day) was administered. The piperacillin-tazobactam (13.5 g/day), sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim (3.84 g/day), and ganciclovir (0.5 g/day) were given to treat the lung infection. After 2 months, the patient's lung infection was in remission. However, the patient's urine protein level was still within the nephrotic-range proteinuria. At the ninth month of treatment, the patient was treated with 160 mg per week telitacicept for 8 weeks. Telitacicept was administered in combination with MMF (500 mg/day), HCQ (200 mg/day), and prednisone (10 mg/day). After 8 weeks (eleventh month) of telitacicept treatment, the urine protein-to-creatinine ratio reduced from 5,600 to 3,856 mg/gCr. Serum ALB increased from 30.9 to 38.9 g/L and serum creatinine was stable. Level of immunoglobulin G decreased from 3.76 to 2.91 g/L. Then telitacicept reduced to 80 mg once per week. After 4 months (fifteenth month) of telitacicept therapy, the urine protein-to-creatinine ratio reduced significantly from 3,856 to 1,376 mg/gCr. Serum ALB improved from 38.9 to 42 g/L and level of immunoglobulin G increased from 2.91 to 4.21 g/L. After 6 months of telitacicept treatment (fifteenth month), the urine protein-to-creatinine ratio reduced significantly from 5,600 to 1,376 mg/gCr. During follow-up (from ninth to twenty-first month), the patient's renal function and proteinuria were stable, and there were no apparent manifestations of infection (Fig. 1).

subjective.chief_complaint: A 25-year-old woman with biopsy-proven class IV+V lupus nephritis presented in the seventh month of immunosuppressive therapy with acute fever and cough.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Two years earlier, the patient had presented with facial and lower limb edema, renal insufficiency (serum creatinine 150 μmol/L), nephrotic-range proteinuria (24-h urine protein 12.77 g), hypocomplementemia (low C3), and positive ANA, anti-dsDNA, anti-Sm, and anti-U1RNP antibodies; renal biopsy confirmed class IV+V lupus nephritis (activity index 9, chronicity index 1). She received three pulses of intravenous methylprednisolone (500 mg/day) followed by multitarget oral maintenance with prednisone (30 mg/day), mycophenolate mofetil (MMF 1,000 mg/day), and tacrolimus (2 mg/day). After 4 months, serum creatinine improved to 73 μmol/L and anti-dsDNA/ANA turned negative; MMF was stopped due to infection concerns, and she was maintained on tacrolimus (4 mg/day), hydroxychloroquine (200 mg/day), and prednisone, with persistent nephrotic proteinuria (UPCR 3,834.33–8,590.89 mg/gCr) and hypoalbuminemia (22.7–32.8 g/L) at month 6. In the seventh month of treatment, she developed acute fever and cough.
subjective.past_medical_history: Systemic lupus erythematosus with class IV+V lupus nephritis diagnosed 2 years prior, treated with pulse methylprednisolone, oral prednisone, mycophenolate mofetil, tacrolimus, and hydroxychloroquine.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for fever and cough at month 7; baseline history of facial and lower limb edema. Home medications at onset of pneumonia included tacrolimus (4 mg/day), hydroxychloroquine (200 mg/day), and prednisone.

objective.physical_examination: Initial baseline presentation 2 years prior notable for facial and lower limb edema.
objective.routine_investigations: Baseline lupus nephritis workup: Serum creatinine 150 μmol/L (normal: 41.00–81.00 μmol/L), improving to 73 μmol/L at month 4; 24-h urine protein 12.77 g; UPCR 5,665 mg/gCr (3,834.33–8,590.89 mg/gCr at month 6); serum albumin 22.7–32.8 g/L; positive baseline ANA, anti-dsDNA, anti-Sm, and anti-U1RNP with low C3. Month 7 pneumonia workup: Elevated procalcitonin (PCT) and C-reactive protein (CRP); positive serum cytomegalovirus (CMV)-IgM.
objective.advanced_workup: Baseline renal biopsy: Class IV+V lupus nephritis (activity index 9, chronicity index 1). Month 7 chest CT and peripheral blood metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS): Demonstrated pulmonary infiltrates and Pneumocystis jirovecii sequences diagnostic of Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PJP).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PJP; confirmed by chest CT and peripheral blood next-generation sequencing) with concurrent cytomegalovirus (CMV-IgM positive) co-infection in a patient with class IV+V lupus nephritis on tacrolimus and prednisone. Plan and clinical course: Tacrolimus and oral prednisone were discontinued, and she was treated with low-dose methylprednisolone (8 mg/day), sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim (3.84 g/day), ganciclovir (0.5 g/day), and piperacillin-tazobactam (13.5 g/day). Her pulmonary infection achieved complete remission after 2 months. At month 9, to treat persistent nephrotic-range proteinuria (UPCR 5,600 mg/gCr) safely after PJP recovery, subcutaneous telitacicept (160 mg weekly for 8 weeks, then 80 mg weekly) was added to low-dose MMF (500 mg/day), hydroxychloroquine (200 mg/day), and prednisone (10 mg/day), reducing her UPCR to 1,376 mg/gCr and normalizing serum albumin to 42 g/L by month 15 without any recurrent infections through 21 months of follow-up.
